gap: No result ChatGPT got states that MonsGeek's own FAQ says the FUN60 drops to a 100 Hz polling rate on 2.4 GHz when the backlight is switched off with Fn + L (power-saving mode), and that keeping 8K with the lights down means dimming to the lowest level with Fn + [ instead.
standout_why: Compared against mechanicalkeyboard.net (best-budget-hall-effect-keyboard), gamepadsquire.com, mkbguide.com (best-gaming-keyboards-under-100), hlplanet.com and setupinsider.com, all opened 2026-11-21. Between them they already cover most of this angle: mkbguide gives per-mode polling for the Epomaker HE65 V2 TMR and HE60 (8,000 Hz USB and 2.4 GHz, 125 Hz Bluetooth) and socket limits for nearly every board; gamepadsquire says the AULA F75 HE's 2.4 GHz mode tops out at 1,000 Hz and the FUN60 Ultra TMR keeps 8,000 Hz on wired and 2.4 GHz; setupinsider says Redragon's magnetic switches are not compatible with other brands. What they lack is narrow: the FUN60's lights-off 100 Hz exception, and any per-mode polling or socket statement for the Gamakay boards (hlplanet lists the NS68, NS75 and TK75HE V2 with switches and prices only). I could not fill the Gamakay half from Gamakay's product pages (HTTP 429 on every attempt), so the only new maker-sourced fact is the MonsGeek one.
decides: It does not change the pick. It adds a caveat to a wireless MonsGeek FUN60 row (ChatGPT's first-run #1): the 8K-on-2.4 GHz claim holds only with the backlight on or dimmed, not off. For our linkable Gamakay NS75, the one Gamakay document I could open claims 8,000 Hz for wired only and is silent on 2.4 GHz and Bluetooth, so the page should say '8,000 Hz wired (Gamakay)' for it and not claim wireless 8K unless another agent reads the product page or manual.

findings.label: Polling rate on 2.4 GHz with backlight off
findings.source_title: MonsGeek FAQ: Why Does the Polling Rate Differ with Backlight On and Off in 2.4G Mode on FUN60?
findings.note: Maker's words: "In 2.4G mode, pressing Fn + L to turn off the lights activates the power-saving mode, reducing the polling rate to 100Hz." The FAQ shows no publication date and does not distinguish FUN60 variants; it says the same applies to the M1 V5 TMR wireless models.

findings.label: How to keep 8K on 2.4 GHz with lights down
findings.value: Dim the backlight to its lowest level with Fn + [ instead of turning it off
findings.source_title: MonsGeek FAQ: Why Does the Polling Rate Differ with Backlight On and Off in 2.4G Mode on FUN60?
findings.note: Maker's words: "If you need 8K polling rate but want the lights off, use Fn + [ (FUN 60)". The FAQ gives no figure for wired or Bluetooth.
